messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: KV cache memory spike detected on hosted-runtime-us-east-1. Current mem usage 92% across pool-3. Auto-escalation to on-call started. thread:1958889999

pagerduty-bot: Paging @sanjay (runtime oncall) — incident #INC-2026-1243 (kv-cache context leak).

sanjay: I’m on it. seeing sustained growth in KV entries since ~1958887500. likely a long-prompt/prefix amplification.

emma: customers reporting elevated latency and some 503s for chat endpoints. support says 5 customers with >5min errors. @support-bot any customer list?

support-bot: Affected customers: acme-inc, quickdocs, noteflow. All on hosted tier, mostly long-context workloads. Ticket links: https://tickets.internal/ACME-123, https://tickets.internal/ND-456

alex: grabbing node heap/dump now. quick grep on traces shows many entries with sequence_length > 64k and repeated prefetch keys. suspect prefetch window not bounding when prompts include very long single-line histories.

liz: Are we seeing continuous batching amplify this? if large prefetched KV remains, batching will group, causing memory amplification.

sanjay: yes. continuous-batcher is still batching max_batch_size 64, and prefetch_readahead 8. A runaway prompt created N prefix entries leading to per-request kv growth x10. Need immediate throttle.

emma: mitigation path options: 1) rollback prefetch rollout, 2) toggle prefetch_readahead to 1 globally (hotfix), 3) enable aggressive eviction (ttl 30s) on pool-3, 4) fallback to smaller model for affected routes. Thoughts?

alex: quickest safe change is config toggle to set prefetch_readahead=1 and continuous-batching max_batch_size=16 on pool-3. I can push a runtime config override to hosted-runtime-us-east that takes effect in ~30s.

sanjay: do it. also enable kv-cache soft-eviction max_keys_per_session=1024 as temporary cap. that prevents infinite growth.

alex: patching now — applying override: ```
PATCH /admin/runtime/configs/pools/pool-3
{
  "prefetch_readahead": 1,
  "continuous_batching": {"max_batch_size": 16},
  "kv_cache": {"soft_eviction_max_keys_per_session": 1024}
}
```

alex: override applied. waiting for propagation. monitoring mem and error rates.

liz: logs show immediate drop in new KV insert rates. baseline mem usage trending down from 92% -> 76% in 2 minutes.

sanjay: throttled new prefetched entries. still some backfill from backlog but error rate for chat endpoints dropping.

emma: support — tell customers we’ve applied a temporary mitigation that reduces prefetch aggressiveness and will continue to monitor; ETA for full fix?

support-bot: Notifying affected customers with status: mitigation applied, investigating root cause, will update in 30m.

alex: next step: reproduce locally with long single-token prompts and see why prefetch doesn't cap keys. suspect bug in prefix dedupe when whitespace > 64k.

sanjay: onboarding a short-term fix into runtime: ensure prefetch rejects sessions with prefix_length > 32k, and add metric for keys_per_session. I’ll open a PR and nominate for hotfix rollout.

liz: also add a guard in continuous-batching to refuse batch grouping if total_kv_estimated_bytes > 200MB. prevents batching amplification.

emma: ok team — oncall handoff in 45m. Sanjay will remain lead; Alex will stay for ops until 1958890200. Liz will follow up on instrumentation. I’ll draft incident note.

sanjay: will follow up with postmortem template and customer impact summary. major root cause hypothesis: unbounded prefetch combined with continuous batch grouping created a positive feedback loop for KV growth with very long prompts.

pagerduty-bot: Incident #INC-2026-1243 acknowledged: status=mitigated, severity=high -> monitoring.

emma: closing loop — memory back to ~60% across pool-3, error rates normalized, no new 503s in last 10m. logging this thread to the incidents channel for postmortem. if anyone hits regressions re-open. :white_check_mark:
